Residual-after-M0 sign pattern m=7..13: +,-,+,-,+,-,- (5/6 alternations), geometric mean |ratio|=7.882 vs candidate 1/|lambda2|=8.0872 (2.6% off). Phase 2 (Z06/Z44/Z50, free u_inf, 5 pts each): LOOCV rms abs err improvement factors 313x/527x/485x (M2 over M0'); D amplitudes +4.384/+112.766/+275.028, same sign as Phase 1's D=+0.001985 across all 4 independent nodes. Coordinator independently reproduced this (sign pattern, ratio 7.891, amplitudes to all digits) -- Phase 1/2 audited GREEN.
verdict.degree4_M2: FINAL (Phase 3c, last iteration): STILL NEYASNO / effectively NULL for the two-term sum in the only valid (non-circular) range. Dominant-term claim (lambda2(4) beats delta4) remains CONFIRMED decisively, unchanged throughout.
verdict.degree4_M2_evidence: Phase 3 original (cascade m=7..12, lambda2(4) to ~10 digits): M0 (pure delta4) LOOCV rel err 684% (catastrophic). M0L (pure lambda2(4)^m, single term) LOOCV rel err 0.99% (excellent) -- decisively confirms lambda2(4) dominates over delta4, reproducing quartic pilot's ratio~3.4266 finding. M2 (both terms free) LOOCV rel err 4.1%, WORSE than M0L alone. Phase 3b (20-digit lambda2(4)): essentially unchanged (M2=4.11% vs M0L=0.99%); extending to m=13 made both worse (outlier ratio e4(12)/e4(13)=3.585 vs 3.36-3.46 band). Phase 3c (FINAL): coordinator independently confirmed the m=12/13 outlier is real (audit_a14_check.py, diffs <=4.8e-45, not a precision artifact). Extended to m=7..16 via own-verified cascade k=15,16,17 (dps=140, forward-continuation Newton, exact-period checked, diffs vs pilot 5.5e-46/3.0e-46/4.8e-45). CRITICAL DISCOVERY: a_F in mside_cascade.json is cF_rich[K_MAX=17], algebraically built FROM cascade[15],[16],[17] via the Richardson chain -- so e4(14),e4(15),e4(16) are CIRCULAR (a_F was constructed using the same cascade[k] being tested against it), exactly analogous to agent A's Z72 exclusion in REPORT_LAMBDA2_DEG2.md section 3.3. This explains the striking exact-delta4 ratio observed at m=14/15 and m=15/16 (7.284686217... to 11 digits) as a Richardson-recursion residual artifact, NOT a physical delta4-vs-lambda2 crossover. Re-ran the tail model selection on ONLY the non-circular subset m=10..13 (4 points, k=11..14): none of 4 candidate second terms (delta4^-m, lambda3(4)^m=0.2557, coordinate mode 1/alpha4^m=0.5916, lambda2(4)^2^m=0.0852) beat pure-lambda2 M0L in LOOCV (best was coordinate mode at 0.0365 vs M0L's 0.0316 -- still worse). CONCLUSION: consistent null result across all three sub-phases (3, 3b, 3c) in every non-circular range tested -- no second term is resolvable for degree 4 with the available data; this is now well-established rather than a lingering precision question.

CRITICAL_circularity_finding.issue: a_F = cF_rich[K_MAX=17] = (cF_seq[17]-r2*cF_seq[16])/(1-r2); cF_seq[17]=f(cascade[17],cascade[16]); cF_seq[16]=f(cascade[16],cascade[15]) -- a_F is ALGEBRAICALLY built from cascade[15],[16],[17] (traced directly from quartic_pilot/p3_mside.py source).
CRITICAL_circularity_finding.consequence: e4(14) [k=15], e4(15) [k=16], e4(16) [k=17] compute (cascade[k]-a_F) with a_F constructed FROM that same cascade[k] -- circular. The exact-delta4 ratio at m=14-16 is a Richardson-recursion artifact, not physics. Analogous to agent A's Z72 exclusion (REPORT_LAMBDA2_DEG2.md 3.3).

question1_does_M2_beat_M0L_now.answer: NO in both cases. Precision increase alone (10->20 digits) makes no material difference on the original range; extending the range makes both models worse (dominated by an apparent outlier at m=12/13).

question2_delta4_amplitude_C.note: C on m=7..12 is stable and consistent with the original run's C=0.424239 (same sign, <0.03% shift). C on m=7..13 jumps by ~9x (3.77 vs 0.42) purely because of the m=13 outlier point dragging the 2-parameter fit -- NOT read as a reliable amplitude estimate; the m=7..12 value is the more trustworthy one.

m7to12_subset_preferred.reading: |C| < ~1.6 (conservative), or C consistent with 0 within +/-1.5-1.7 at 2 sigma -- a real bound, D/C-scale comparison: |D|=0.0379 so this bound does not itself rule out a delta4 term at amplitude comparable to or even somewhat larger than D; it just says the present 6-point data cannot resolve it.

m7to13_full_range_looser.reading: much looser/noisier bound, dominated by the m=13 outlier -- the m=7..12 bound above is preferred.

phase3_deg4_quartic.limitation: lambda2(4)=0.2918380893 (brief, ~10 digits) vs quartic_fixedpoint.json checks.eigen2_deflated=0.29183840898354510453 (~6-7 digit agreement only) -- insufficient precision to resolve the subordinate delta4 term once the dominant lambda2(4) term (99% of signal) is accounted for.
